---
title: "Depression and Nutrition - NHANES"
author: "Stephen He"
format: pdf
editor: visual
---

The document uses and presents open-access data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from CDC's National Center for Health Statistics. It a source for reviewing and analyzing statistics on population health through national population surveys conducted from 1990 to the present day in the United States.

For the purpose of this research project, we are interested in the data from the Mental Health- Depression Screener, stored in the Questionnaire Data from each NHANES study period. We are also interested in the data containing the food codes and the diet overview (macronutrients and micronutrients consumed) from the Dietary Data. The information is collected from the NHANES March 2017-2020 study period, before the COVID-19 pandemic. This is the most recent data that has been completed.

Although the survey does not emphasize psychological well-being beyond states of depression, many data concerning mood and nutrition are restricted from public access, especially those that come from clinical or metabolic cohort studies, which provides greater depth in diet and its impact on behaviour.

## Loading In Datasets

```{r}
#| label: load_and_view_data
library(haven)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(GGally)
library(MASS)
library(broom)
library(randomForest)
library(caret)
library(ggfortify)

dietary_interview_first24 <- read_xpt("P_DR1IFF.xpt")
dietary_interview_first24 |> glimpse()

#food_codes <- read_xpt("P_DRXFCD.xpt")
#food_codes |> glimpse()

demographic <- read_xpt("P_DEMO.xpt")
demographic |> glimpse()

depression <- read_xpt("P_DPQ.xpt")
depression
```

First, we can remove any variables that aren't relevant to the analysis (but still worth considering when interpreting and processing the results).We are primarily interested in the nutrient intake and the types of food consumed, and the psychological response to the diet choices, which are the moods related to depression.

Additionally, the data from Food Interview of the Dietary Data and the Demographic Questionnaire will be subsetted to participants who were 18 years and older during the time of screening. This is crucial as the Mental Health- Depression Screener only consists of adult participants. Thus, the analysis of this project represents adult participants from the United States who volunteered to take part of the NHANES study during March of 2017 to 2020.

```{r}
#| label: clean_and_subset_data

dietary_interview_first24_subset <- subset(dietary_interview_first24,
                                           select = c(-WTDR2DPP, -DR1EXMER, -DR1DRSTZ, -DR1EXMER, -DRABF, -DR1DBIH, -DR1DAY, -DR1LANG, -DR1_030Z, -DR1FS, -DR1_040Z))

dietary_interview_first24_subset

demographic_age <- demographic |> dplyr::select(SEQN, RIDAGEYR)
demographic_age

age_diet_interview <- left_join(dietary_interview_first24_subset, demographic_age, by = "SEQN")

age_diet_interview_adults <- age_diet_interview |> filter(RIDAGEYR >= 18)
age_diet_interview_adults
```

We will also remove any variables from the demographic questionnaire that are not relevant to the analysis.

```{r}
#| label: Subsetting_demogrpahic_data
demographic_subset <- subset(demographic, select = c(-SDDSRVYR, -RIDSTATR, -RIDAGEMN, -RIDRETH1, -RIDRETH3, -RIDEXMON, -DMDBORN4, -DMDYRUSZ, -DMDEDUC2, -RIDEXPRG, -SIALANG, -SIAPROXY, -SIAINTRP, -FIALANG, -FIAPROXY, -FIAINTRP, -MIALANG, -MIAPROXY, -MIAINTRP, -AIALANGA))
```

In the Mental Health- Depression Screener, we need to observe the number of missing values for each of the 10 questions.

```{r}
depression |> 
  map(~ .x |> is.na() |> sum()) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  enframe(name = "Variable", value = "Number NA") |> 
  mutate(
    `Proportion Missing` = `Number NA` / 8965
  ) |> 
  adorn_rounding(3)
```

Now, we can clear the N/A values.

```{r}
#| label: Removing_missing_values
demographic_clean <- demographic_subset |> na.omit()
depression_clean <- depression |> na.omit()
```

Now, with the depression screener data, we can categorize ranges of the PHQ-9 scores into different levels of severity.

```{r}
#| label: Adding_new_column_that_represents_depression_severity_based_on_score_range
depression_clean <- depression_clean  |> 
  mutate(
    total_phq9 = DPQ010 + DPQ020 + DPQ030 + DPQ040 +
      DPQ050 + DPQ060 + DPQ070 + DPQ080 + DPQ090, 
    depression_severity = case_when(
      total_phq9 <= 4 ~ "None",
      total_phq9 <= 9 ~ "Mild",
      total_phq9 <= 14 ~ "Moderate",
      total_phq9 <= 19 ~ "Moderately severe",
      total_phq9 <= 27 ~ "Severe"
    )
  )
depression_clean
```

```{r}
depression_clean <- depression_clean |> filter(total_phq9 <= 27) |> 
  mutate(
    depression_severity = fct(depression_severity, levels = c("None", "Mild", "Moderate", "Moderately severe", "Severe"))
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: Distribution_of_depression_scores_among_participants
depression_clean |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = total_phq9)) + 
  geom_histogram(colour = "white", bins = 10) + 
  labs(x = "Total Score", y = "Number of Participants", title = "Distribution of PHQ-9 Scores Among All Participants")
ggsave("PHQ9_distribution.png")
```

```{r}
depression_clean |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = depression_severity)) + 
  geom_bar() + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.5)) + labs(x = "Depression Severity",
                                                                    y = "Number of Participants", title = "Proportion of Depression Severity")
ggsave("Prop_depression.png")
```

```{r}
#| label: Combining_and_adding_SEQN_for_all_macronutrients

#In this dataframe, we have all SEQNs that participated in the diet interview
age_diet_adults_macro <- age_diet_interview_adults |> 
  group_by(SEQN) |> 
  summarize(
    across(c(DR1IKCAL, DR1IFIBE, DR1ICHOL, DR1IPROT, DR1ICARB, ends_with("FAT")), sum)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: Distributions_of_macronutrient_consumption_among_participants
age_diet_adults_macro |> dplyr::select(-DR1IKCAL, -DR1ICHOL) |>
  pivot_longer(-SEQN) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) + 
  geom_histogram(colour = "white", bins = 20) + 
  facet_wrap(~ name, scale = "free_x") + labs(x = "Amount of the Macronutrient Consumed (gm)", title = "Distributions of Macronutrient Consumption Among Participants")
 
#ggsave("Macronutrient_historgrams.png")
```

It appears that most of the data lies to the right, violating normality and indicating right skews.

## Combining PHQ-9, Dietary Data, and Demographic Data Together

We can now add up all identical SEQN numbers and treat them as one person (since they are), and include all their macronutrient data together (since the interview represents one day of food intake). Then, we can include the cleaned depression screener and demographic data into `completed`.

```{r}
#| label: Grouping_all_SEQN_for_macronutrient_consumption_and_adding_depression_and_demographic_data
completed <- age_diet_interview_adults |> 
  group_by(SEQN) |> 
  summarize(
    across(c(DR1IKCAL, DR1IPROT, DR1ICARB, DR1IFIBE, DR1ICHOL, ends_with("FAT")), sum), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  right_join(depression_clean, by = "SEQN") |> left_join(demographic_clean, by = "SEQN") |> mutate(RIAGENDR = factor(RIAGENDR, labels = c("Male", "Female"))) |> na.omit()
```

Gender, (`RIAGENDR`) is a discrete binary variable, 1 being Male, and 2 being Female. It is of interest to navigate how age, gender, and family income ratio appears in the analysis.

```{r}
#| warning = FALSE
#|label: Proportions_of_depression_severities_among_male_and_female_participants_
completed |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = depression_severity, fill = factor(RIAGENDR))) + 
  geom_bar(position = "dodge", aes(y = after_stat(prop), group = RIAGENDR)) + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.5), plot.axis = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)) + labs(fill = "Gender") + labs(x = "Depression Severity for PHQ-9 Scores", y = "Proportion", title = "Proportions of Depression Severity") + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent)

#ggsave("Prop_of_depression_severities_with_gender.png")
```

```{r}
#| message: FALSE
#| label: An_example_of_PHQ-9_scores_against_protein_consumption
depression_mood <- lm(total_phq9 ~ DR1IPROT, data = completed)

completed |> ggplot(aes(x = DR1IPROT, y = total_phq9)) + geom_jitter() + geom_smooth(method = "lm") + labs( x = "Protein Consumption (gm)", y = "Total PHQ-9 Score", title = "The Relationship Between Protein Consumption and Depression Scores") + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12), axis.title = element_text(size = 12))

ggsave("Regression_prot_depression.png")
```

This behaviour is almost identical to carbohydrate and fat consumption, revealing a strong right skewness.

## Producing Additive Model of all Variables

```{r}
completed_sub <- completed |> dplyr::select(total_phq9, starts_with("DR1I"), RIDAGEYR, INDFMPIR, RIAGENDR)
mod <- completed_sub |> lm(total_phq9 ~ ., data = _)

summary(mod)
```

```{r}
interaction_mod <- completed_sub |> lm(total_phq9 ~ DR1IFIBE * INDFMPIR * DR1IPFAT * DR1IMFAT, data = _)

summary(interaction_mod)
```

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE
#| message: FALSE
set.seed(88114)
library(glmnet)
library(rsample)
library(recipes)
library(parsnip)
library(workflows)
library(dials)
library(tune)


#Splitting testing and training data
data_split <- initial_split(completed_sub, prop = 0.70, strata = "total_phq9")

train <- training(data_split)
test <- testing(data_split)

#K-fold cross validation, randomly splits data in 10 groups
folds <- vfold_cv(train, v = 10, strata = total_phq9)

lasso_recipe <- recipe(total_phq9 ~ ., data = train) |>
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |> #GEMINI
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |> # Convert charactesr or factors into binary
  step_zv(all_predictors())            |> # Removes variables that only have one single value, those with no variance
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) # cnter and scale numeric variables for Lasso

#Constructing lasso model with a selection penality, tuning to find the best value for predictions
lasso_model <- linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 1) |> set_engine("glmnet")

# Putting the lasso model into a workflow()
lasso_wf <- workflow() |> add_recipe(lasso_recipe) |> add_model(lasso_model)

#A grid is made to list a set if penalty values that would be the most optimal for variable selection
lasso_grid <- tibble(penalty = 10^seq(-4,-1, length.out = 30))

lasso_grid |> top_n(-5)
lasso_grid |> top_n(5)

lasso_tune_results <- tune_grid(
  lasso_wf,
  resamples = folds,
  grid = lasso_grid, control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE))
#The 30 penalized regression models are trained using tune_grid()


# Visualise the performance across different penalty values
autoplot(lasso_tune_results)

#GEMINI

# Extract the numerically best penalty
best_penalty_term <- select_best(lasso_tune_results, metric = "rmse")

# Update the workflow with the best penalty
final_lasso_wf <- finalize_workflow(lasso_wf, best_penalty_term)

# Fit to training data and evaluate on test data in one step
final_fit <- last_fit(final_lasso_wf, data_split)

collect_metrics(final_fit)

extract_fit_parsnip(final_fit) |> tidy()






```
